block.title: Rocq prints captured instructions as SSA in an Iris goal
block.p: The Hello capture puts the directory allocator and the locale alias comparison in one file. Rocq accepts two other spellings of both functions by reflexivity. Abbreviations reduce the file from 5,234 bytes to 4,391. A custom grammar for instructions and jumps reduces it to 4,177 bytes.

Rocq 9.3.0 compiled all three files in 0.38 seconds on swa. Their compiled objects ranged from 12,548 to 12,695 bytes. Each time is the median of six runs after warmup, with the notation modules already compiled. Repeating both functions sixteen times in one file gave medians of 0.79 seconds for constructors, 0.76 for abbreviations and 0.73 for SSA notation.

In an Iris weakest-precondition goal for the allocator, rq goals printed these instructions from the original capture after we unfolded the block. The short addition applies when the base pointer also supplies the lower bound. Rocq prints both operands in a full flight when the donor differs.

Byte literals reduced the source for glibc’s error-name table from 6,890 bytes to 4,515. Rocq checked the whole initializer by reflexivity, including the zero after each name. The compiled object grew by 17 bytes.
With Rocq and its standard library on the path, run python3 nanofil/bench/rocq-notation/run.py --copies 16 to repeat the comparison.
